key: IPCC AR6 WGIII Chapter 12: Cross-sectoral Perspectives (Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change) || July 2023 Cambridge University Press publication (identical content to April 2022 IPCC release). No update or erratum issued. AR7 not expected until ~2028. However, the draft quotes the IEA Net Zero scenario as deploying DACCS at '0.6 GtCO2 in 2050', multiple IEA and third-party sources consistently report the IEA NZE DAC figure as ~980 MtCO2 (~0.98 GtCO2) in 2050, not 0.6 GtCO2. This figure-level discrepancy requires verification against the exact passage in Ch.12 — it may reflect a different IEA scenario vintage or a transcription error in the draft

key: Lamb WF et al. 'The carbon dioxide removal gap' — Nature Climate Change || The paper was published 3 May 2024 (online) / June 2024 (issue) in Nature Climate Change vol. 14, pp. 644–651 — not 2023 as the draft states. A follow-up commentary by Lamb et al. ('Countries need to provide clarity on the role of carbon dioxide removal in their climate pledges') appeared in Environmental Research Letters in November 2024. The State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026), co-led by Lamb, contains a dedicated CDR gap chapter (Chapter 9) that updates the gap analysis using NDCs submitted through September 2025 and finds the 2030 CDR gap is 0.3 GtCO2/yr against a median Paris-compatible scenario level of 2.9 GtCO2/yr, and that the gap is 'large and growing' toward 2050

key: Minx JC et al. 'Negative emissions—Part 1: Research landscape and synthesis' — Environmental Research Letters 13 (2018) 063001 || The 2018 paper has not been retracted or formally superseded by a direct replacement article. However, the IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022) and the State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026, Edwards et al., doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRD65) now constitute the authoritative updated synthesis of the same research landscape. No newer version of the Minx et al. Part 1 paper itself has been published. The qualitative conclusions the draft draws from it are broadly consistent with the 2022 and 2026 assessments, but the 2018 paper's scenario base is now eight years old

key: Fuss S et al. 'Negative emissions—Part 2: Costs, potentials and side effects' — Environmental Research Letters 13 (2018) 063002 || The State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026, Edwards et al., doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRD65) contains a dedicated Chapter 10 on costs and potentials that provides updated estimates for all major CDR methods using literature through 2025. The IPCC AR6 WGIII Chapter 12 (2022) also updated the potential ranges. The 2018 Fuss et al. figures are now eight years old and have been substantially revised in subsequent assessments — for example, the State of CDR 3rd Edition reports novel CDR currently at ~0.002 GtCO2/yr growing at ~40% annually, and updated cost and potential ranges differ from the 2018 estimates across multiple methods
